Double-centre a distance matrix

Source: R/svt.R
dblctr.Rd

\(B = -\frac{1}{2} H D^{(2)} H\) with \(H = I - n^{-1} 1 1'\) and \(D^{(2)}\) the squared distances: the inner-product matrix of classical scaling (Torgerson 1952).

Usage

dblctr(D)

Arguments

D

A symmetric matrix of distances.

Value

A list of class dblctr with the matrix B.

References

Torgerson, W. S. (1952). Multidimensional scaling: I. Theory and method. Psychometrika, 17(4), 401-419. doi:10.1007/BF02288916

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

D <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(c(0, 1, 3, 4), c(0, 1, 0, 2))))
dblctr(D)$B
#>         [,1]    [,2]    [,3]    [,4]
#> [1,]  4.5625  1.8125 -1.4375 -4.9375
#> [2,]  1.8125  1.0625 -1.1875 -1.6875
#> [3,] -1.4375 -1.1875  1.5625  1.0625
#> [4,] -4.9375 -1.6875  1.0625  5.5625
